title: Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
authors: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham
abstract: We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.
summary: This theoretical paper provides sharp, high-order approximations for the magnetization of mixed spherical spin glasses operating in the replica symmetric phase. By extending analysis beyond simple quadratic models to include cubic disorder, the authors achieve an error bound of $o(N^{-1/2})$. This work is significant for applications requiring extreme accuracy in statistical physics models, such as stochastic localization techniques.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive highly accurate approximations for the Gibbs measure of mixed spherical spin glasses, specifically achieving an error bound of $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate.
main_result: It provides an explicit coordinatewise expansion for the magnetization vector, including the leading cubic disorder correction, and a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector.
method: The analysis combines techniques from complex analysis, including Laplace transforms and saddle-point approximations, with rigorous bounding of error terms using concentration inequalities.
model_or_system: The system studied is a mixed spherical spin glass governed by a Hamiltonian $H_{N}^{p,q}(\sigma)$, which is analyzed in the replica symmetric phase.
key_observables: Magnetization vector ($\langle \sigma angle$), resolvent response to the external field, and high-moment estimates of the magnetization.
important_parameters: The analysis is valid in the replica symmetric phase, assuming weak external fields ($\langle u angle \le c_0 \sqrt{N}$), and requires the replica symmetry condition $\xi_{p,q}^2 \ll 1$.
main_assumptions: The results rely heavily on the replica symmetry assumption and the ability to control error terms using exponential decay bounds, particularly when perturbing away from purely quadratic models.
paper_structure: The paper develops by first analyzing quadratic models using Laplace transforms and saddle-point methods (establishing preliminary lemmas). It then extends this analysis to include cubic disorder terms, deriving the coordinatewise expansion (Theorem 2.1), and finally proving the full high-moment bound (Theorem 2.2) by controlling error terms through concentration inequalities.
why_interesting: While focused on spin glasses, the rigorous mathematical techniques developed for error control and high-order moment estimation are highly relevant to analyzing complex quantum many-body systems where standard mean-field approximations fail.
